candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, and Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, and hell shall give back that which it owes' — the resurrection of the dead in Enochic apocalyptic. The three-way restitution (earth gives back bodies; Sheol gives back righteous spirits; hell gives back the wicked) anticipates the New Testament resurrection accounts. The Tewahedo eschatological tradition draws explicit cross-reference: 1 Enoch's resurrection vision pre-dates the Pharisaic-Pauline development and provides the canonical Jewish textual basis for the doctrine. The Mäṣḥafä Hēnok is read liturgically in Tewahedo funeral rites for precisely this verse's hope.

candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And the Elect One shall in those days sit on My throne, and his mouth shall pour forth all the secrets of wisdom and counsel: for the Lord of Spirits hath given them to him and hath glorified him' — Elect-One-on-My-throne. Tewahedo Christology emphasizes the SHARED-throne (Heb 1:3-8; Rev 3:21, 22:1-3) as continuous with this Enochic image: the Son shares the Father's throne not as conquest but as eternal counsel.
